subject: Re: Great House Farm
source: Original email in the family's Gmail (read-only export); contact details redacted.
text:
Dear Mr Buckler,

I have undertaken a reasonable search of our records and would advise 
you as follows:

a) The minutes of all council minutes for the period in question were 
deposited in the Glamorgan Records Office in 2002. These cover the 
period from 1982 when Llandough Community Council was first formed. 
Prior to that time, the community of Llandough was included in the remit 
of Penarth Town Council. The relevant web-link which shows the 
information held is : perihttps://glamarchives.gov.uk/od

b) You are able to visit the Glamorgan Records Office in Cardiff by 
appointment and the web-link to find details of their location is: 
https://glamarchives.gov.uk/

Section 21 of the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) is an absolute 
exemption that allows public authorities to refuse a request if the 
requested information is already reasonably accessible to the applicant 
by other means. This avoids duplicating effort and prevents authorities 
from acting as personal research services.

c) I would suggest that you access the Llandough Community Council's 
website for historical information about the community of Llandough - 
web-link is :

https://www.llandough-cc.co.uk/Buildings_of_Significance_in_our_Community_25590.aspx

Kind regards,

Paul R. Egan BA, Chartered MCIPD, CiLCA, F. Inst. LM, FIPSM

> Sir/Ma'am,
> 
> I am your constituent, living in Dinas Powys. I am writing to request 
> your assistance in reviewing a historic legal matter involving my 
> family: _BP Properties Ltd v Buckler (1987)_, relating to Great House 
> Farm, Llandough.
> 
> My family lived on, cared for and claimed to own that farm for 
> generations. The events surrounding the 1987 case resulted in the loss 
> of our home and land, and left several members of my family deeply 
> affected. Recent research I have undertaken has revealed significant 
> procedural inconsistencies, historical irregularities, unanswered 
> questions regarding corporate identity, unverified service of key 
> documents, and heritage considerations relating to the site.
> 
> I have attached a short report summarising SOME of these issues. I am 
> requesting your help in identifying the appropriate bodies--legal, 
> historical, or governmental--who may be able to independently review 
> the historical record to ensure fairness, accuracy, and transparency.
> 
> My interest is not solely personal; Great House Farm has a heritage 
> significance to Wales, including documented accounts that Guglielmo 
> Marconi stayed there while experimenting with early radio technology. I 
> believe this should form part of our preserved historical record.
> 
> By way of background, I am a veteran and have served both in the Armed 
> Forces and recently with the Vale of Glamorgan Council. My intention is 
> simply to seek clarity, proper review, and justice where appropriate. I 
> would be grateful for your guidance on the correct avenues to pursue.
> 
> Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to your 
> response.
> 
> Yours sincerely,
